I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go down.

Going down would leave both cell (5,5) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
The line must go right: up is number 6, which comes later.
Going right would leave both cell (1,5) and cell (3,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and number 5 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
